wire.scope: Independent checksum/TCP/Hello/outer-record framing and absence of public HTTP plaintext. Actual endpoint SSL establishes decrypted HTTP bytes; serial labels alone never establish authentication. Malformed/partial/certificate-negative modes make no TLS close_notify or TCP FIN claim.

dns.scope: Independent full captured Ethernet/IPv4/UDP lengths and checksums, exact query/response bytes, fixed endpoint and finite ticket/transaction binding. IPv4 UDP zero checksums are explicit. Host send attempts are distinct from packets; no DNS cache, public resolver, web, TLS, physical containment or pixel claim.

resolution.scope: Exact positive DNS RELEASE precedes retained BEGIN_STREAM_RESOLVED admission; bounded admission time is observed in serial. Subsequent egress hash/length joins the actual first TCP SYN, which follows the actual captured DNS answer. DNS observation is provenance data under held BOOT authority and fixed endpoint policy, not DNS authenticity or new authority.

document.scope: Actual fixed BOOT-controlled HTTPS document through fresh held policy/seed/UTC/DNS/duplex authority; real endpoint OpenSSL and independent ciphertext capture plus complete bounded reader glyphs. Public laboratory root only; no host proxy, publicInternet/publicCA, arbitrary endpoint, HTML, physical/SMP/hostile-containment or daily-driver acceptance claim.

configuration.scope: Immutable BOOT metadata and scalar checked copy; held device authority is checked separately. Route holder obtains no NIC metadata; gateway data alone is separate from the transport route receipt.

routing.scope: Normal-profile private default-route receipt after held BOOT metadata and device readiness. Actual next-hop bytes and neighbor recovery require independent wire evidence.

self_wait.scope: Sampled real BOOT/main-task/park/timer/Ring3 receipts with explicitly caller-selected observed Browser task IDs; no identity autodiscovery or authority grant. Native peer and desktop gates separately establish useful progress. Nominal timer-assisted polling, not NIC IRQ, CPU/power bound, physical or SMP proof.
